Information since June points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, with inflation running below the symmetric 2% objective and market-based inflation compensation remaining low. In sticky-price New Keynesian frameworks (e.g., Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005; evidence on sluggish price adjustment in Nakamura and Steinsson), subdued inflation and anchored expectations warrant lowering policy rates to reduce real rates and support demand. The 25 bp cut to a 2–2.25% funds-rate range and the earlier end to balance-sheet runoff are consistent with estimated Fed reaction functions (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and a risk-management approach when global headwinds raise downside risks. The noted softness in business fixed investment aligns with financial-frictions evidence (Bernanke and Gertler) that investment is sensitive to external finance premia; easing seeks to mitigate that channel. Operationally, adjusting interest on reserves and using ON RRP within the corridor/floor system fits the post-2008 implementation framework (Goodfriend, 2002). Overall, the statement is cautiously accommodative and supportive of continued expansion while acknowledging uncertainties.
